consensus_findings.description: Critical: three capability directories under `openspec/contracts/` have no `openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` — `phase-record`, `project-context-refresh`, and `prototyping` (verified: `ls openspec/contracts/` vs `ls openspec/specs/`; the spec tree has `project-context-refresh-orchestration` and `project-context-refresh-records`, no `project-context-refresh`). specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md 'The gate fails closed on malformed input' makes exactly that state a hard failure ('a capability directory containing contract documents but no capability spec SHALL fail'), with no opt-in escape — the fail-closed requirement is not gated on D6 or D13. Task 5.7 wires the full sweep as push-blocking on `main`. So merging this change reds `main` on the first push, on three capabilities the change never touches. The root cause is documented policy, not an accident: `openspec/contracts/README.md` organizes by short capability label ('Capability = short label'), while D2 assumes `<capability>` is a directory name under `openspec/specs/`.

Critical: the term 'contract document' is used 20+ times across specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md, design.md D6/D10/D12/D13 and tasks.md, and is never defined anywhere in the change. It is load-bearing twice over: forward opt-in is keyed on the document (D6), and the fail-closed rule is keyed on 'a capability directory containing contract documents'. The real tree makes the ambiguity concrete: `openspec/contracts/` currently holds `*/schemas/*.schema.json` (13 of them), `gen-eval-framework/cli/gen-eval.yaml`, and `code-search/v2.yaml` — a full OpenAPI 3.1 document sitting at the capability root rather than under `openapi/`, contrary to `openspec/contracts/README.md`'s own layout table. After task 4.2b the tree also gains `gen-eval-framework/traceability-exclusions.yaml`, which a naive `**/*.yaml` discovery glob would itself parse as a contract document. No requirement, design decision, or task states the discovery rule, so the implementer of task 3.7 picks it silently — and the pick determines finding 1's severity.

Critical: D13's reverse switch has no fail-closed rule, so the direction D3 calls the valuable one fails open. Reverse enforcement is keyed on the mere existence of `openspec/contracts/<capability>/traceability-exclusions.yaml`, and the requirement 'The gate fails closed on malformed input' covers only contract documents, schema-invalid traceability blocks, and missing capability specs — it never mentions the exclusions file. An exclusions file that is unparseable YAML, schema-invalid, an empty file (YAML `None`, which the schema rejects because `exclusions` is required), or unreadable therefore reads indistinguishably from 'not opted in', and the capability's reverse completeness silently stops blocking. This is precisely the failure the same requirement's own rationale identifies for the forward direction ('a parse error that reads as "no blocks found" would silently downgrade a traced contract to untraced'), left unextended to the switch introduced one iteration later. Task 3.6's four bullets have no malformed-exclusions-file case. It also quietly inverts the precedent D4 claims to lift 'wholesale': `packages/gen-eval/scripts/check_coverage_completeness.py` lines 163-176 fail on a MISSING exclusions file ('a missing X is not a passing one') and separately fail on malformed YAML naming the file.

Critical: cross-capability exclusions are permitted by the contract and unspecified by the spec. `contracts/traceability-exclusions.schema.json` documents the `requirement` field as 'Usually this capability's own prefix; a cross-capability exclusion is permitted and appears in the cross-capability report', but no requirement, scenario, design decision (D4, D9, D13) or task says whether capability A's exclusions file suppresses capability B's reverse-completeness failure. If it does, it is a laundering path — the proposal's risk table mitigates exactly that risk for cross-capability CITATIONS (report them as a distinct list, D9) and leaves the exclusion side unmitigated, which is worse because an exclusion asserts nobody needs to serve the requirement at all. It also relocates D4's stale-exclusion failure onto an owner who cannot see the cause: A's exclusion goes stale when B rewords a heading. If it does not suppress, the schema's description is simply false and will be implemented as written by whoever reads the schema first.

Critical: the skill tests wp-wiring must add will never run in CI. `skills/tests/validate-feature/` is NOT listed in `skills/pyproject.toml`'s `testpaths` (verified by grep; the list ends at `expedite/scripts/tests` and includes `tests/implement-feature`, `tests/plan-feature`, `tests/validate-packages` but not `tests/validate-feature`), and CI's `test-infra-skills` job runs a bare `uv run pytest` from `skills/`, which honours `testpaths`. The existing `skills/tests/validate-feature/test_gen_eval_mode_selection.py` is already invisible for this reason. So the skill-workflow ADDED scenario 'Skill wiring is covered by skill tests' would be satisfied by a suite CI never executes — the pyproject's own comment names this defect verbatim ('A test CI never runs fails the same way as one that always passes'). wp-wiring's verification step runs the path explicitly so package verification passes, which makes the gap invisible until long after merge. `skills/pyproject.toml` is in no package's `write_allow`.

Critical: task 2.0 invalidates a generated artifact no package may write. Promoting `traceability.schema.json` and `traceability-exclusions.schema.json` to `openspec/contracts/gen-eval-framework/schemas/` changes the output of the `api.contracts` producer, which renders a deterministic inventory of every `openspec/contracts/**/*.schema.json` into `docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md` (see `skills/project-context-refresh/scripts/producer_api_contracts.py`: `_INVENTORY_TARGET`, `_schema_files` rglob, and a rendered header line carrying the COUNT — currently `_13 contract schema(s)._` plus one table row per schema including each `$id`). Two more schemas make it 15 with two new rows, and the `context-drift-gate` CI job (`make context-drift-gate`, exit 2 = blocking drift) reds. `docs/architecture-analysis/contracts-inventory.md` appears in no package's `write_allow`, so the implementer of wp-model has no in-scope way to fix the gate it just broke. This is a DIFFERENT instance from the one the gatekeeper flagged — see finding 15, where the gatekeeper's specific claim is refuted.

Critical: the change flips gen-eval-framework into blocking reverse enforcement (task 4.2b) and installs the blocking main sweep (task 5.7) in the same PR, and nothing requires the unmutated tree to pass at capability scope before merge. Task 4.3 proves the gate goes RED on two documented mutations; that is the falsifiability half. The GREEN half — `check_traceability.py --scope capability` exiting zero across every capability on the merge candidate — appears in no task, no verification step, and no acceptance outcome. Measured scale of the triage 4.2b must complete for that to hold: `openspec/specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md` has 20 archived requirements, this change's own delta adds 14 more (all about the gate itself, none with any CLI surface, so each needs a written exclusion), and task 4.1 adds roughly one per contracted flag (17). That is ~51 requirements to cite-or-excuse inside one task sized `[M]` (2hr–1day).

Nit: the new skill-workflow requirement 'Validation-Time Requirement Traceability Gate' is unconditional — `/validate-feature` SHALL run `check_traceability.py` and SHALL fail validation on non-zero — but `skills/validate-feature/SKILL.md` is a shared payload that `install.sh` ships into consumer repositories that have neither `packages/gen-eval/scripts/check_traceability.py` nor `openspec/contracts/`. There is no gate-unavailable scenario. Either the skill hard-fails everywhere downstream, or it silently skips and the blocking gate becomes decoration in the repos it was installed into. The same skill already solves this correctly one phase up: the `gen-eval` phase auto-detects descriptors and prints an explicit `SKIP: No gen-eval descriptors found` line (SKILL.md ~lines 293-312). That the boundary is real and linted is confirmed by `skills/validate-feature/scripts/linters/dependency_direction.py`, which treats `.md` as a runtime file and flags canonical `skills/...` and `skills/.venv` paths inside skill payloads.

Critical: D13 assigns reverse enforcement ownership to the capability at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/design.md D13 lines 429-468 and spec lines 202-217, but openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/contracts/traceability-exclusions.schema.json lines 18-22 explicitly permits cross-capability requirement exclusions. That lets a file under capability A excuse capability B's requirement, creating a state B cannot own: B may be reverse-enforced while A suppresses its gap, or B may be not opted in while A's file changes B's reported completeness.

Critical: D12 claims the full sweep can block merges while specifying CI on main as push-triggered at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/design.md lines 363-366, and task 5.7 repeats that at tasks.md lines 493-498. A push event on main runs after a merge has already landed, so it can red main but cannot block the merge it is meant to guard.

Critical: wp-wiring's dispatch precondition is only prose at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/work-packages.yaml lines 384-390, while the machine-readable depends_on list at lines 394-396 includes only wp-gate and wp-matrix. The scheduler can dispatch wp-wiring before human tasks 4.1, 4.2, 4.2b, and 5.2 land, making the real-artifact RED demonstrations impossible or fixture-only despite the plan saying that is invalid.

Critical: D6's document-total forward commitment and D13's reverse opt-in switch are not reflected in D12's change-scoped touched set. design.md D12 (lines 368–375) and specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md "Validation-time evaluation is scoped to the change" define touched operations as only those whose contract *nodes* changed, and touched requirements as ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED plus those named by citations/exclusions the diff adds or changes. That means (a) adding the first `traceability`/`x-traceability` block to one operation opts the whole document into forward enforcement (D6 / scenario "Declaring traceability commits the whole contract document") while change-scope only fails the edited node—sibling uncited operations in the same file are not touched and do not fail; (b) creating `traceability-exclusions.yaml` (possibly empty) opts the capability into reverse enforcement (D13) while change-scope only fails requirements named by that file or added by the change—other uncited requirements stay non-blocking until the main sweep. This is exactly an "opted in but not blocking on the newly enforced surface" path at `/validate-feature`, which D6/D12/D13 claim to make impossible as a configuration outcome. tasks.md 3.15 only proves pre-existing gaps in already-traced surfaces, not opt-in transitions.

Critical: The gate's fail-closed posture for contracts is not mirrored for the reverse-opt-in artifact. specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md "The gate fails closed on malformed input" and tasks.md 3.6 cover unparseable contracts, schema-invalid operation blocks, missing capability specs, and specs without contracts—but neither the requirement nor tasks 3.4/3.6 specify behavior when `openspec/contracts/<capability>/traceability-exclusions.yaml` exists yet is unreadable, non-UTF8, invalid YAML, missing the required `exclusions` key, or schema-invalid. Under D13 that file's existence *is* reverse opt-in; treating a broken file as absent is fail-open (reverse not enforced while authors believe they opted in), and treating it as present with zero exclusions without validating shape is a different silent decision. check_coverage_completeness.py's load_exclusions already fails closed on bad exclusion files—this change claims to reuse that shape but does not specify the same hardness for the reverse switch.

Nit: D13 gives the reverse direction an all-or-nothing switch and no staging mechanism, which strands the capability the change was motivated by. D10 gives forward a staging path (split the document, opt in per subsystem) and D10 itself concedes 'the reverse direction was never split-stageable in the first place'. The consequence is stated but not costed: agent-coordinator — where the proposal's headline measurement lives (10 requirements naming an operation the app does not serve) — cannot opt in without triaging all 122 requirements in one step, so task 5.2 defers it and no roadmap item claims it. The direction D3 argues is the valuable one, because nothing else in the repository detects it, will in practice be enforced for exactly one capability. D13 considers three alternatives (implied-by-any-document, standalone boolean, the file itself) but not a SUBSET declaration — the exclusions file naming which requirement groups or heading prefixes it certifies — which is not flippable-without-work (the certification is still per requirement) and does stage.

Nit: two requirements give contradictory answers for a capability holding an exclusions file and no contract documents. 'The gate fails closed on malformed input' says 'a capability with a spec and no contracts SHALL be recorded as untraced ... the run SHALL NOT fail on it'; 'Reverse enforcement is opt-in per capability via the exclusions file' says reverse SHALL be enforced 'exactly when' the file exists. The state is reachable — the exclusions file lives under `openspec/contracts/<capability>/`, so creating that directory solely to hold it is the natural first move for a capability whose requirements are all served elsewhere or excluded. Under one reading the capability is recorded untraced and passes; under the other every requirement must be cited or excluded. The word 'untraced' is doing double duty as a per-document forward status and a per-capability status.

Nit: task 5.5 identifies the hand-fill-instruction-survives-the-generator hazard and then names only one of the two files carrying that instruction. `openspec/schemas/feature-workflow/templates/change-context.md` lines 13-14 say 'Phase 1: Fill Req ID, Spec Source, Description, Contract Ref, ...' and 'Contract Ref: path to contract file the requirement maps to (e.g., contracts/openapi/v1.yaml#/paths/~1users)'. The task's note covers `skills/implement-feature/SKILL.md` only, and the template appears in no package's `write_allow`, so wp-matrix cannot fix it even if the implementer notices. The template is the artifact an author actually copies, so leaving it stale is the more consequential of the two.

Nit: `deny: openspec/contracts/**` on wp-gate, wp-matrix and wp-wiring reproduces the exact defect the plan iteration just removed elsewhere. PLAN_ITERATE dropped `deny: openspec/specs/**` from every package on the grounds that deny beats read_allow in `IndexScopes.allows` and bought nothing on writes. Verified: `skills/validate-packages/scripts/context_impact.py` lines 174-178 — `if _matches_any(path, self.deny): return False` before consulting `read_allow`. The identical argument applies to `openspec/contracts/**`: none of the three packages has any `write_allow` entry under that tree, so the deny cannot prevent a write that `write_allow` does not already prevent, while it does remove the entire contract tree from the read/context scope of wp-gate — the package implementing `check_traceability.py`, whose default `--contracts-root` IS `openspec/contracts/` and which needs `gen-eval-framework/cli/gen-eval.yaml` as its reference for what a real traceability block looks like.

FYI: three other in-flight changes add requirements to `gen-eval-framework` — `extract-gen-eval-package` (6), `factory-missions-architecture-alignment` (3), `rename-descriptor-model-levels` (2). Once task 4.2b creates `openspec/contracts/gen-eval-framework/traceability-exclusions.yaml`, that capability is reverse-enforced, so each of those changes will fail its own change-scoped validation run until it cites or excludes its new requirements (the scenario 'A requirement the change adds and nobody cites fails the change-scoped run' fires). That is the ratchet behaving as designed and is not a defect, but their authors planned before the switch existed and will meet it as an unexplained validation failure.

Nit: openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md:474 - Requirement 'The gate fails closed on malformed input' specifies fail-closed behavior for unparseable contract documents and schema-invalid blocks, but omits specifying behavior when openspec/contracts/<capability>/traceability-exclusions.yaml is malformed, unparseable, or present-but-unreadable.

Nit: openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/work-packages.yaml:372 - Package wp-wiring specifies a DISPATCH PRECONDITION in prose requiring human tasks 4.1, 4.2, and 4.2b to land before dispatch, but its depends_on array lists only [wp-gate, wp-matrix]. Automated DAG orchestrators executing strictly by depends_on would dispatch wp-wiring prematurely.

Critical: The malformed-input requirement at openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md lines 474-520 covers malformed contracts and traceability blocks, but not malformed, empty, schema-invalid, or unreadable traceability-exclusions.yaml files. D13 makes that file's existence the reverse opt-in switch, so an unreadable or unparsable switch artifact must fail closed rather than being treated as absent, empty, or reporting-only; task 3.4 at tasks.md lines 225-236 also lacks that RED case.

Critical: Two scenarios assign opposite exit behavior to the same capability shape. specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md scenario "A capability with a spec and no contracts is untraced" (requirement "The gate fails closed on malformed input") requires the run SHALL NOT fail. Scenario "The exclusions file's presence enforces reverse completeness" (requirement "Reverse enforcement is opt-in per capability via the exclusions file") requires failure when any requirement is uncited and not excluded, with no contracts prerequisite. A capability that has a spec, zero contract documents, and a present `traceability-exclusions.yaml` (including `exclusions: []`) satisfies both WHEN clauses and cannot both pass and fail. Task 3.4's "file present with empty list → every requirement must be cited" and task 3.6's untraced-no-contracts case inherit the contradiction.

Critical: Cross-capability requirement exclusions are permitted by the schema but have no evaluation semantics. contracts/traceability-exclusions.schema.json (property `requirement`, lines 19–21) allows any `<capability>.<slug>` and says a cross-capability exclusion "is permitted and appears in the cross-capability report." design.md D9 and the reverse-completeness scenarios only define credit for cross-capability *citations*, not exclusions. If capability A's exclusions file can excuse B's requirements toward B's reverse completeness, A can launder B's reverse gaps without B owning the triage—the coupling D9 reports rather than fails for citations becomes a silent veto-free excuse for exclusions. If foreign ids do not count, the schema description is wrong and the gate should fail them as invalid/stale for this file.

Critical: wp-wiring's DISPATCH PRECONDITION is prose-only and invisible to the package DAG. work-packages.yaml `wp-wiring` (description lines 384–390) says do not dispatch before human tasks 4.1/4.2/4.2b land because RED demos for 5.6/5.7 mutate real gen-eval artifacts; `depends_on` is only `[wp-gate, wp-matrix]`. tasks.md 5.7 depends on 3.16 and 5.2 but not 4.2/4.2b, while 5.6 depends on 4.2 but not 4.2b—so reverse flagship state required by the package text is not in either graph. The scheduler can legally dispatch wiring against fixtures only, which is the mirror-verification failure mode this change exists to end. Human tasks are intentionally excluded from packages (work-packages.yaml lines 440–450), so there is no package edge that can express the precondition without a new mechanism.

Nit: the concentration denominator can be zero and the spec does not say what happens. 'The gate reports citation concentration deterministically' fixes the denominator as 'the capability's traced operations' and D7 repeats it. A capability that has opted into reverse enforcement but whose contract documents are all untraced has zero traced operations, which is reachable and in fact is the natural first state of a capability opting in reverse-first. Task 3.9's fixture (six traced operations, four citing one requirement) never exercises it.

Nit: the change's own spec delta contains an uncited requirement, in a change whose thesis is that requirements must be cited by what serves them. The skill-workflow MODIFIED requirement '3-Phase Incremental Generation' gains four new AND clauses in its Phase 1 scenario (Contract Ref generated from citations; join by parse position; no name re-matching; no hand-fill when a traced document exists), and no task's `**Spec scenarios**` line references 'Phase 1 — Test plan (pre-implementation)'. Tasks 5.4 and 5.5 implement exactly those clauses and cite only `D8`. Cross-checked mechanically: every other scenario in the change is referenced by at least one task; the three MODIFIED skill-workflow scenarios are the only unreferenced ones (the three ADDED ones are covered by 5.6's 'all three scenarios').

The plan iteration's refutation of the gatekeeper's wp-model write_allow suggestion is correct, verified empirically rather than accepted. (a) `packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/contracts/interface-descriptor.schema.json` has exactly these `$defs`: AuthConfig, BudgetConfig, CommandSpec, EndpointSpec, FileInterfaceMapping, McpToolSpec, ServiceSpec, StartupConfig, StateVerifier. FlagSpec, PositionalSpec, ToolCommandSpec, ExitCodeSpec, BindingSpec and OperationSpec are all absent, because `generate_contract_schemas.py` generates from `InterfaceDescriptor` alone while `ToolDescriptor` and `ServiceDescriptor` are SUBCLASSES that add those fields. Adding an optional `traceability` field to the four archetype-only models therefore cannot move a byte of that schema. (b) `generate_tool_descriptor.py` dumps flags, positionals and commands with `model_dump(mode="json", exclude_defaults=True)` (lines 121, 129, 136), so a field whose default is the absent value keeps `evaluation/descriptor.yaml` byte-identical until a contract actually carries a citation — at which point task 4.2 already requires regeneration. The gatekeeper's suggested widening should NOT be applied; widening write scope would have licensed exactly the drift those two `--check` gates exist to catch. The correct constraint is the model-placement rule now written into task 2.2 and wp-model's description.

D2's empirical claims hold exactly, reproduced independently. Implementing the normative slug algorithm as written (NFKD, drop combining marks, lowercase, collapse runs outside [a-z0-9] to a single `-`, strip leading/trailing `-`) over all 29 `openspec/specs/*/spec.md` files yields 632 requirement headings, of which 0 produce an identifier failing `traceability.schema.json`'s `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*\.[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` citation pattern, and 0 intra-capability slug collisions. Both figures match the design's stated 632 and zero. That makes task 1.1's instruction to drive the check against every real spec — rather than a fixture authored alongside the resolver — both achievable today and the right discriminator.

Optional: `work-packages.yaml` declares no `context_impact` block on any of the five packages. Under ri-08 that records `unmigrated` rather than failing, so nothing breaks. But this change touches four of the six declared surfaces per `openspec/schemas/context-impact-rules.yaml`: `apis` (`openspec/contracts/**`, `**/*.schema.json`), `capabilities` (`openspec/changes/*/specs/**`), and `documentation` (`**/*.md`, `**/SKILL.md`). A change specifically about making contract-to-requirement impact explicit, declining to declare its own context impact, is an odd asymmetry — and finding 6 is a concrete instance of the drift the declaration exists to surface.

Mechanical checks that pass, recorded so a later reader knows they were run rather than assumed. `openspec validate trace-requirements-to-contracts --strict` → valid. `validate_work_packages.py` → VALID on all four checks (schema, depends_on_refs, dag_cycles, lock_keys). All 14 ADDED requirements in the gen-eval-framework delta carry SHALL on their FIRST line, which is the only line `--strict` inspects. The skill-workflow MODIFIED requirement heading `3-Phase Incremental Generation` matches the archived base at `openspec/specs/skill-workflow/spec.md:1548` exactly, preserves all three base scenarios, and drops no base AND clause — so the archive merge will find its base. Every `**Design decisions**` reference in tasks.md resolves to a decision defined in design.md, and every one of D1–D13 is referenced by at least one task. Every parenthesised `**Spec scenarios**` reference resolves to a real scenario heading. The RED-demonstration protocol is stated once at the top of tasks.md and referenced thereafter rather than restated per task, which is why the two wired-gate demonstrations in the final checkpoint are unambiguous.

The strongest structural property of this plan is that its central negative is a task rather than a comment. Task 2.3 ('an operation whose name and path almost exactly match a requirement heading must still cite nothing') is the only test that can detect the single change — a helpful fuzzy matcher — that would make the entire gate worthless while leaving every other test green. D1, D2's display-only ranking caveat, D8's join-by-parse-position rule and D11's RENAMED fail-open analysis are four independent statements of the same invariant at four different layers, each with its own test. That is the correct shape for a gate whose failure mode is a false negative that looks like coverage.

FYI: openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/design.md:427 - Assessment of Design Decision D13 (Directional Opt-in): D13's separation of forward (per contract document) and reverse (per capability) opt-in is architecturally sound and resolves staging deadlocks. Overloading traceability-exclusions.yaml as the reverse switch ensures reverse enforcement is only activated after full requirement triage, though it prevents incremental recording of requirement exclusions before complete capability triage.

FYI: openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/work-packages.yaml:120 - Evaluation of the wp-model write scope dispute: Empirical verification confirms the plan's refutation is correct. FlagSpec, PositionalSpec, ToolCommandSpec, and OperationSpec are archetype-only models unreachable from InterfaceDescriptor. Adding an optional traceability field with default None to these models does not alter interface-descriptor.schema.json (verified via generate_contract_schemas.py --check) and exclude_defaults=True preserves byte-identity of evaluation/descriptor.yaml (verified via generate_tool_descriptor.py --check). Expanding write_allow is unnecessary.

openspec/changes/trace-requirements-to-contracts/specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md:1 - Spec quality verification: All 14 ADDED requirements in gen-eval-framework/spec.md and 2 MODIFIED/ADDED requirements in skill-workflow/spec.md contain SHALL on their very first line, passing strict validation via openspec validate --strict.

The wp-model refutation is supported by the repository evidence: generate_contract_schemas.py renders InterfaceDescriptor only at packages/gen-eval/scripts/generate_contract_schemas.py lines 80-90; InterfaceDescriptor reaches ServiceSpec/EndpointSpec/McpToolSpec/CommandSpec at descriptor.py lines 191-271, not FlagSpec/PositionalSpec/ToolCommandSpec or service_descriptor.OperationSpec. generate_tool_descriptor.py uses exclude_defaults=True on command, flag, and positional payloads at lines 118-137, so an optional traceability field with default None should not drift evaluation/descriptor.yaml until real traceability blocks are added and the human retrofit regenerates it.

Nit: Stale-exclusion wording does not match the operation-side schema. specs/gen-eval-framework/spec.md scenario "A stale exclusion fails the gate" (and the parent requirement text) says an exclusion naming "a requirement identifier or operation that no longer exists" fails. contracts/traceability.schema.json `excluded` only has `reason`—it does not name an operation; the exclusion is attached to the operation node, so when the operation disappears the exclusion disappears with it. The stale check that D4/tasks.md 3.3 need is meaningful for requirement-side entries in traceability-exclusions.yaml (and for requirement ids that no longer resolve), not for a free-standing operation id in an exclusion list.

Nit: contracts/README.md still claims splitting the coordinator surface "costs nothing in rigour" (section "Not in this directory", lines 58–61). design.md D10 (lines 298–307) explicitly corrected that earlier claim: splitting stages *forward* only; reverse is whole-capability via D13 and was "never split-stageable." The README wording is a pre-D13 leftover that can re-teach the wrong staging model to implementers of task 5.2.

FYI: Verdict on D13 (directional opt-in). design.md D13, the reverse-opt-in requirement/scenarios, proposal acceptance outcomes, tasks 3.4/4.2b/5.2, and contracts/traceability-exclusions.schema.json are mutually consistent: forward opts in per document via block presence (D6); reverse opts in per capability via exclusions-file presence; empty list means full reverse strictness. The D12 distinction is real, not a rationalization—D12 forbade a second switch for the *same* claim's blocking bit; D13 switches a different claim with a different owner. Grep of the change directory found no residual single-switch "capability opts into both directions" rule after plan-findings F1. The overloaded artifact does make one state inexpressible (record requirement-exclusion reasons without reverse enforcement); that is an intentional adoption cliff, mitigated by report-without-file for uncited requirements, and is acceptable for gen-eval-scale triage—but only if finding #1's change-scope transition hole is fixed so "create the file" cannot mean "opted in yet not fully checked at validation."

The plan's refusal to widen wp-model write_allow for packages/gen-eval/src/gen_eval/contracts/** and evaluation/descriptor.yaml is correct on the merits. Empirically: (1) packages/gen-eval/scripts/generate_contract_schemas.py render() builds interface-descriptor.schema.json only from descriptor.InterfaceDescriptor (lines 80–85); InterfaceDescriptor.model_json_schema $defs contain AuthConfig/BudgetConfig/CommandSpec/EndpointSpec/FileInterfaceMapping/McpToolSpec/ServiceSpec/StartupConfig/StateVerifier and do *not* include FlagSpec, PositionalSpec, ToolCommandSpec, or OperationSpec—verified via model_json_schema. ServiceSpec nests EndpointSpec/McpToolSpec/CommandSpec only; FlagSpec/PositionalSpec/ToolCommandSpec hang off ToolDescriptor.commands, and OperationSpec hangs off ServiceDescriptor.operations—neither archetype-only tree is walked by --check (ci.yml ~411). (2) generate_tool_descriptor.py _flag_payload/_positional_payload/_command_payload use model_dump(mode="json", exclude_defaults=True) (lines 114–143); a default-None traceability field is omitted from dumps (verified), so evaluation/descriptor.yaml stays byte-identical under --check (ci.yml ~431) until a contract actually carries non-default citations—which task 4.2 already requires regenerating as human work outside wp-model. Widening write_allow would be unnecessary surface area.

Gate falsifiability and RED protocol are unusually strong for a plan. tasks.md defines a concrete RED-demonstration protocol (lines 10–17); phase 3 maps failure modes to pytest files; tasks 3.1–3.6/3.9/3.11/3.13/3.15 each require non-zero exit and naming; task 4.3 mutates real flagship artifacts both forward and reverse; the final checkpoint requires recorded exit codes for both wired gates. Citation concentration is deterministic via CONCENTRATION_REPORT_SHARE (D7) so its test is not a self-mirror. Scope fail-closed (unresolvable merge base / missing --change) is specified and tasked. Residual gaps are the opt-in-transition and exclusions-file parse cases in findings 1–2, not a general "gate only observed to pass" problem.
